subject.title: Feature request: Escalating stall recovery for sub-agents (nudge → kill)

question: Should this subagent nudge-to-kill request stay as a standalone default-on subagent recovery feature, or be folded into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101863's bounded-liveness design?
rationale: Current main has partial session-level active-abort recovery, while the remaining request adds new recovery policy, possible config/defaults, child-run mutation, and channel-visible behavior that need maintainer product direction before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into Run-Lifecycle Design
options.body: Use this issue as subagent-specific acceptance evidence under the bounded-liveness and terminal-release direction, and implement only through the shared RunActivity/terminal-outcome contract.

options.title: Approve Standalone Subagent Watchdog
options.body: Define separate subagent inactivity thresholds, nudge content, kill semantics, and parent/channel notification behavior outside the broader lifecycle umbrella.

options.title: Treat Active-Abort As Enough
options.body: Confirm that current diagnostics active-abort plus future general liveness work replaces subagent-specific nudge/kill, then close or narrow this issue.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Run-Lifecycle Design
recommendation.body: Use this issue as subagent-specific acceptance evidence under the bounded-liveness and terminal-release direction, and implement only through the shared RunActivity/terminal-outcome contract.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus owns the overlapping run-lifecycle reliability umbrella that now decides whether this specific subagent recovery request is standalone or folded into the broader design.
